idiom_name: indirect enum with associated values + a children computed property
implementation_notes: In Swift the idiomatic realization is an indirect enum whose cases carry the node-specific data (the indirect keyword boxes recursive cases) plus a computed children property implemented by one switch arm per case; switch over an enum is exhaustive by the compiler, so per-node dispatch needs no visitor. Reference semantics are the alternative when nodes must be shared or mutated in place - SwiftSyntax, the official Swift parser library, uses a generated class hierarchy with children(viewMode:) for exactly that reason - but for a hand-written DSL tree the enum is the direct form.
pitfalls: Enum cases are value types: assigning a node copies its case, and shared subtrees need an explicit reference box (indirect only makes recursion legal, it does not make sharing cheap).
children allocates an array on every access; expose forEachChild or cache when a pass visits the same nodes repeatedly.
A default arm in the switch over an enum disables the compiler's exhaustiveness check and silently swallows cases added later.
